title: Job sat in ashes wondering why his life had collapsed.
paragraphs: Job sat in ashes wondering why his life had collapsed.

His wealth was gone.
His children were gone.
His body was covered in painful sores.
And heaven seemed silent.
But what Job never knew was that his suffering had started with a conversation in heaven.
Satan accused him.
“He only serves You because You bless him.”
In other words: Take away the blessings… and the faith will disappear.
But God knew something Satan did not understand.
Job’s faith was not built on comfort.
It was built on devotion.
So while Job sat on the ground scraping his wounds, believing God had abandoned him, heaven was watching something extraordinary.
A man who refused to curse God even when his life collapsed.
One of the most powerful lines in Scripture appears in Job 1:21:
“The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.”
Job never knew his suffering was answering an accusation.
He never knew his faith was being witnessed in heaven.
And sometimes, the same may be true for us.
Some trials are not punishment.
Some trials are proof.
Proof that faith is real.
Proof that devotion is deeper than blessing.
Proof that even in loss, God is still worthy.
You may not understand why you are walking through a difficult season.
But there may be a story unfolding above you that you cannot see.
Your faith might be answering a question you never heard.
Because some of the greatest victories of faith happen in battles we never fully understand.
Do you think God sometimes allows trials to reveal the depth of a person’s faith?
